r.notes: I reported on a small female with these conditions last year, and this could be her again. The paws were closed across the chest, so couldn't see gland markings. I rang Redlands Wildlife Ambulance immediately, but when they arrived, the koala had moved. We all searched the area, but couldn't find her. I found fresh urine and Megan found the small, pale green scats next to the urine. The urine had the distinctive odour of cystitis. I used to smell it all the time when the little female was around last year. Ambos tried twice last year to catch her then, but she bolted for the canopy each time.

Delighted to actually hear him after all year with only 1 record. The numbers of calls in one go was over 20, so wondered if it was  Pavarotti  from last breeding season. Pav usually calls up to 60 times in the one session. This male made no noise in the inhale, only the usual exhale noise, but he was gripunting away for over 20 times after I started counting
Seen this koala several times recently in this area
koala was in pergola area
Walked through property towards adjacent Harrington Reserve
reported to KAG by email

Koala was screaming. I'Ve never before heard a female screaming without a male nearby grunting. How sad that there is no alpha male is this area for this breeding season. First time in 10 years here this has happened. Developers have finally got their wish - no more koalas. Heartbreaking.
Reported by Redlands Care Network to RAWA
Every year at this time we hear a male koala grunting.  I've been here for 12 years and each year have heard him. It fills my heart with joy to know he's still around
Delighted to actually hear another koala, as there have been so few this year. No alpha male in this area, for the first time in 10 years!
Saw pop on the footpath so looked up and was in the tree closest to the footpath/road
Unusual to hear a female screaming the mating scream, without hearing a male there as well.
Sounded exactly like  Pavarotti heard earlier this month and 2018 breeding season. His bellowing sessions are very extensive - heard 19 repetitions before I came inside.

The group of trees where the koala was, is just a small isolated pocket along a drain/creek,  surrounded by houses. In Carmay Close, the bush area extends from #4 to  #7. There are only about 5 gums and several young Melaleucas, as well as a forest of young Macaranga seedlings.
Koala first seen 7.50 am and was in fork of tree all day. Couldn't determine sex.
Sounded exactly like Pavarotti male from around here last breeding season. So named for his extensive bellowing repetitions - I counted over 50 in one session last year!!!
So few this year - heartbreaking.
I would see koalas about twice a year on our property
Sounds like a new male, as very different grunting pattern and duration. Only a couple of bellows

I've heard a few lately ( see reports) - perhaps attracted by the large container of fresh water, I've placed at the base of a large  E. tereticornis over the back fence. I've certainly heard wallabies stopping near the water I put out. I keep topping it up, so good sign.
Known resident koala to property owner, ear tagged and observed over last few years.
From the grunting pattern, which is very prolonged, it sounded like the same male who has been around for the mating season.
This is the first sighting/hearing since November! Can the continuous heat be affecting the koalas or are they gone?
Semi-regularly seen in this area and on this property. Koala previously seen on the street/roadside in November. Property is part of Koala Conservation Agreement Program.
Sounded like the usual male from this season. He's in fine form tonight - very persistent and moving quite fast
Close to the road, high in a tree and on the bank of Eprapah Creek in Eprapah forest/Charles S. Snow Reserve.
Didn't sound like the usual highly enthusiastic and persistent bellowing of the  male we've had this season. This male gave only 3 tired sounding grunts and gave up!
Koala not seen, only heard grunting. T sounded like the usual male from the recent breeding season. He has a distinctive and very persistent grunting pattern.
Possibly female; alert, active, climbed to near top of large gum
Report emailed to KAG
Sighting emailed to KAG Admin
Report emailed to KAG Admin
First time we have seen koala here. Koala about 20m up.
Recorded on facebook page 'Wild in the Redlands'
I here him throughout the year.  I know he's around because of his grunting.
Fairly large joey
In same tree, large joey about 3 m above female.  Both alert. Same pair seen in same area 30 September 2023.
Emailed to KAG.  Reporter states seen occasionally but not as much as previously
Has been around for the last month
This is the second Koala we have noticed on our property, which we purchased in October 2020.
Once again, Pavarotti’s distinctive calling pattern. This time 37 reps, after his introduction. Good to know he’s still around.
Pavarotti again with his usual vocal athletics. He was in full voice when I first heard him and continued for only 26 reps until he moved away, still grunting.
Notified Wildlife Rescue Volunteers accordingly
It sounded like “Pavarotti” again. This time 27 inhale/exhales before he stopped! Wonderful to know he’s still around.

From the extensive calling, it sounded like “ Pavarotti “, a male who called up to 50 inhale/exhale in s single session! I’m delighted that he is actually still alive, as I rarely see or hear any at all the last 2 years.
From the calling pattern, I think it was Pavarotti of the sustained bellowing. Last night 37 repetitions, after I started counting and before he moved away. Quite unique call pattern.
He sounded like the unique pattern and lengthy calling of “ Pavarotti” with over 27 grunts sequences, after I started counting.
This sounded like the same grunting pattern of the male that I’ve been hearing lately, not the distinctive “Pavarotti” male.

Doug’s camera shows more detail, but I’ll attach the ones from my IPad. Koala looks small, can’t see chest markings or testicles and head and nose shape would indicate female. Never seen a koala in this particular tree before.
This was a different male, to the usual “Pavarotti” I hear often lately. Very different grunting pattern.
This male had a completely different call duration and pattern to the male heard heard early  this morning and reported earlier.
Bushland area on private property, mostly Scribbly Gum and mid-late stage she-oak forest near drainage line and dam. Property in RCC Koala Conservation Agreement Program.
From the unique grunting pattern and number of repetitions -27 tonight before he moved away, I think it was “ Pavarotti” back again. Wonderful to know he’s still active.
Located near local traffic that had incidents before were kangaroo life were killed
From the call pattern, I think it was “ Pavarotti” of the extended calling. He did 17 repetitions, after I started to listen, before moving away, still bellowing!
Wonderful! 2 koalas in one day.
Reoorted to KAG via FB.  Video footage of koala provided but unable to upload
From the distinctive calling pattern, it was “ Pavarotti” This time he did 35 repetitions before moving away.
Small koala - ? juvenile, ?female. I was just driving into Jeff St, so couldn’t stop to photograph it.
Sunshine Coast uni koala reseachers are studying this property hoping to GPS track koalas.  This female is thought to be Kim with a red ear tag released onto the property about 3 years ago.

Koala not seen, only heard. Sounded like the usual male, but tonight only a cursory round of grunting, not the usual marathon. This is the first time I've heard or seen one this year! Most unusual to go so long with no sightings.
Comes and goes few days and returns for a night and leaves.
Reported to KAG by email. Crossed the road at Panorama Drive and into Carlingford Drive then went up a gum tree in the bush near 14 Carlingford Drive.

From the extensive calling duration, I’m sure it was “ Pavarotti” who is the resident male around here. This set of bellowing/ grunting lasted for 23 repetitions, before he moved away, still bellowing. He is the only koala male that I’ve heard in almost 11 years of reporting,  that continues calling so persistently.
Approximately 75m from Jeff St
Reported to KAG via email. Koala was possibly trying to have a drink from a container in yard
This mother and her baby are near a fairly busy road being Clifford-Perske Drive.
Reported to KAG by email.  Release of koala Bryce  tag 7374
Phone call to KAG with sighting.  First time for several years that reporter has seen a koala in her yard.
Great to actually hear a koala at last. There are now so few left around here.

Although I haven't seen any koalas in the tree, when I checked the large E tereticornis, just over the back fence, 2 days ago, there were very fresh scratches up the trunk. Sometimes at night lately, I have heard the clack of claws as the tree is being climbed. This huge tereticornis always used to be the most used by the various males, over the years, but this year, visits have been very few. Sadly, an all time low.

Koalas not seen only heard bellowing and grunting just behind our boundary fence and right now, a screaming female is yelling her disapproval, at the end of which, the male is giving some low rumbles.

This large tree is on the border of our property and Wellington St (a major road). There are often Koalas who pass through our property to the thin line of trees near this road. A few days before this sighting there was a large male and also a younger male? They were very vocal possibility discussing territory

She is in an E.t only 15mt from where she was last evening. She habitually sits with her left hind leg stuck out, perhaps because her rump is so sore. Can't really see her rump as that area is in shadow, but it is vey dark. No use calling the ambulance as she is much too high - she's extremely wary from previous flaggings.

Apologies for web and stamens across photo. Can't quite see her dirty bottom but that area is extremely dark in photo.Addition - later photo shows it is the female with cystitis. Note left hind leg stuck out as usual.
Koala not seen, only heard bellowing and grunting in usual persistent pattern. Same male as usually recorded.
It was the usual male, not seen, only heard bellowing and grunting his usual persistent pattern .
Koala not seen, only heard bellowing and grunting. The call pattern is identical to all those I have been reporting lately. He has a very persistent, distinctive calling pattern.
Reported to KAG
It sounded like the usual male, who has a distinctive and persistent calling pattern.
Recorder  is a local resident part of Koala Conservation Agreement Program, semi regularly sees koalas in area. Occurrence filmed on phone.
Koala not seen, only heard bellowing persistently as usual.
Koala not seen, only heard persistently bellowing and grunting. Sounds exactly like the same male I've been reporting - very distinctive bellowing pattern.
Reported to KAG email.  Heard only
Have heard them mating over the last few weeks. When we first moved here there were a lot more and mating at night was quite loud.
Heard only
Phone report to KAG
Male not seen, only heard grunting as it moved through the bush
Koala not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing
Female koala not seen, heard screaming and crying
Male not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing. Most unusual after sunrise!
This koala has a big blue tag on her right ear.

Koala not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing. Same male as usually heard - has distinctive grunting pattern. Tonight he's on the Western side of Clifford Perske Dve, along the creek that crosses the road.
Male on ground only heard grunting and bellowing, not seen
Koala not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing. Same male, same distinctive grunting pattern, as earlier this week.
Koala not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing. Same male - distinctive grunting pattern
Male not seen, only grunting and bellowing loudly. Usual male has distinctive grunt pattern
Koala not seen, heard grunting and bellowing in creek line bush
Koala not seen, heard grunting as moved through dry bush
Koala not seen, heard bellowing and grunting
Male not seen, only heard bellowing and grunting. Usual male, but heard in Western side of Clifford Perske Dve, along creek line bush.

Daisy Hill ambulance, and Redlands Wildlife ambulance both tried to capture her for treatment for cystitis and conjunctivitis, previous week. As soon as  flag appeared, she climbed out of reach both times. Haven't seen her since, until today.

Can't really determine gender as attached photo, taken today, seems to show testicles? I took out bowl of fresh water for base of tree and he/she fled up to canopy. Was originally in fork about 7-8 metres above ground. Very wary.
Reported to KAG via email

The koala is certainly female - I saw her chest when she climbed further up the tree, but she is smaller than usual - looks like a juvenile. Wonder if she was the one I heard earlier this week. Wonderful to at last see a koala here again.
This is the first koala sound I've heard for months! Very unusual to go so long without a sighting or hearing them.
I notified the Redlands Wildlife Officers and the wildlife ambulance vols were sent to the area but unable to find the koala.  I had marked the tree with coloured flagging tape.
Haven't seen a koala for about 2 years in this area.Sighting reported to KAG by email

Property is in the Koala Conservation Agreement Program and has observed koalas in the immediate area semi-regularly. Owner noted that it is the first time they had seen them in a while (there is also a recording from early 2018).
Reported to Redlands Wildlife Ambulance
I was delighted to see a mother and baby and wish more was being done in this area to alert residents about our koalas - we used to have so many more.
I can say several times a year we hear him. I've never been able to catch a glimpse because it's always at night.
Emailed to Koala Action Group. In bushland area behind house between Lorikeet Dr and Wellington St

Koala not seen, but heard bellowing and grunting right outside the fence. This is not the same male as last breeding season, as the sound pattern is distinctive. This is the first koala I have seen or heard since 24/4/18! This time last year 37, this year YTD, 8
Hears males regularly

Sounds like the same male reported last time. Have never heard a grunting session last so long! Very distinctive pattern for a least 50 inhale/exhales - I only started counting when he had already been going for ages! Wonderful to hear a koala again, when this year has been virtually devoid of sightings/hearings.
It sounded like the same male heard a week ago. Very distinctive pattern of grunting and very persistent!
Koala not seen, only heard bellowing/grunting Along back fence. Only minimal repititions -5 p, not the marathon grunter, from several weeks ago.
Same koala has been here for six days

Koala only heard heard bellowing/grunting, numerous times before I slept. Sounded like a different one to the one heard earlier in the evening. This was the extended grunts boy - over 30 in the one session!

Koala was same as heard last night - I call him Pavarotti, because of his extremely sustained grunting/bellowing sessions. He was so loud and persistent, he woke me up this morning! He was very vocal all through the night and very close.

First heard the male koala ( persistent bellower) , then the female shortly after he finished bellowing. She was not screaming, but doing the  yoouuu sort of screech/moan. Can't describe it more accurately than that. It's wonderful to finally hear koalas again this breeding season, as there have been so few throughout the year - far fewer than last year.
I think it was female, from size and where she was perched. Usually only the females perch in the outer branches, like she was, in this huge tereticornis.
Both koalas were climbing up the trees, as I could hear the clacking of their claws as they climbed.

I think the koala I reported this morning was indeed female. I saw her more clearly when she switched trees this afternoon. Her coat was very dark, with brown over the shoulders and virtually no white on her back.Male was only heard bellowing and grunting right near her tree.
Koala not seen, only heard grunting and bellowing right behind our back fence. Same male as usual, with distinctive grunting pattern.

This koala was attempted to be captured for cystitis treatment twice earlier this year. She is very wary and heads immediately for the canopy when approached. She is high in this tree's canopy right now, probably catching sun's warmth. Temperature is cool.

Koala not seen, only heard grunting along fence line. First call for several months. Not the usual dominant male from last breeding season. Very different volume and grunting pattern. Actually sounded young and just trying things out, if that's plausible!
Male only heard, not seen. Sounded like an inexperienced  grunting - not very strong or loud and not the usual pattern. Not a male I've heard before. Perhaps a young male trying out?
I took a photo but it wasn't clear.
